summary.oneLiner: Murudeshwar Ceramics Limited manufactures and trades ceramic, vitrified and allied tile products in India, selling through a dealer, architect and builder network under its Naveen tile brand.
summary.business: The Company is engaged in the manufacturing and trading of ceramic, vitrified and allied tile products, with manufacturing facilities at Sira and Karaikal. Its range spans ceramic wall and floor tiles and vitrified tiles including GVT and PGVT in larger formats, sold to residential, commercial and institutional construction demand. Sales are made through an established distribution network supported by dealers, architects, builders and other channel partners.

currentContext.expansion: The Company operates manufacturing plants at Sira and Karaikal. During FY 2025-26 management undertook a comprehensive review of the approved production plan in light of geopolitical tension and conflict (Iran-America, Ukraine-Russia), changing domestic demand patterns, revised customer order forecasts, temporary raw material supply constraints, energy availability and emerging export opportunities. The revised plan is to produce high-value GVT and PGVT vitrified tiles in bigger sizes at the Sira plant and wall tiles at Karaikal, and the Company is planning to produce 60 cm x 60 cm vitrified tile at the Karaikal plant from 1 June 2026. The mix has already moved to larger formats: 60 x 120 cm rose to 53.47% of production in FY 2025-26 from 45.25%, and 80 x 160 cm to 2.62% from 1.41%, while 60 x 60 cm fell to 21.75% from 28.12%. The Directors' Report states the Company incurred capital expenditure of Rs. 5614.67 lakhs during the year, mainly on plant and machinery and building construction, and the MD&A attributes the rise in the debt-equity ratio to 'increase in new borrowings for new project'. The Company also continues energy-conservation investment (energy-efficient equipment, process improvements, monitoring) and adoption of digital printing, surface treatment and process automation technologies.

risks.risk: Raw material and energy cost inflation
risks.note: MD&A Risks & Concerns names fluctuations in raw material and energy costs as a principal exposure; Opportunities & Threats attributes rising energy and raw material costs to Middle East geopolitical tension, the Russia-Ukraine situation and US-initiated trade tariffs, which 'continue to pose challenges to cost management'. Tile manufacture is energy-intensive and the Directors' Report cites energy costs and logistics expenses among the year's challenges.

risks.risk: Competitive intensity and pricing pressure on margins
risks.note: The Company operates in a competitive and dynamic environment against both organized and unorganized tile makers; MD&A states 'competitive intensity, coupled with pricing pressures, may impact margins'.

risks.risk: Demand cyclicality tied to real estate and construction
risks.note: MD&A flags that economic conditions, developments in the real estate and construction sectors, and changes in consumer preferences may impact performance; end-demand is housing, commercial real estate and infrastructure led, so a macroeconomic slowdown transmits directly to volumes.

risks.risk: Supply chain disruption and raw material / energy availability
risks.note: Risks & Concerns lists supply chain disruptions; the production-plan review during the year explicitly identified temporary raw material supply constraints and availability of energy as reasons the approved plan had to be revised.

Credit risks are named in MD&A Risks & Concerns, and the trade receivables turnover ratio deteriorated to 4.46 from 7.12 (a 37.28% variance) with the stated remark 'There is increase in receivable during the year'.

risks.risk: Regulatory, environmental and statutory compliance exposure
risks.note: The business is stated to be subject to regulatory, environmental and statutory compliance requirements, and MD&A adds that changes in government policies and environmental regulations could affect demand and business performance.

risks.risk: Geopolitical conflict and global trade / tariff uncertainty
risks.note: MD&A cites the outbreak of war in the Middle East, the Iran-America and Ukraine-Russia conflicts, US-initiated trade tariffs and uncertainties in global trade as factors that already forced a comprehensive review of the approved production plan and altered customer order forecasts and export opportunities.

The debt equity ratio rose to 0.20 from 0.11, an 84.40% variance, with the stated reason 'There is increase in new borrowings for new project' — the expansion is debt-funded, and the Board withheld a dividend for FY26 to retain profits for working capital and future expansion.
